A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of conventional radiation therapy alone for the management of unresectable stage IIIB non-small lung cancer is no longer appropriate.
the combination of chemotherapy with radiation therapy is superior to chemotherapy alone or radiation therapy alone.
radiation therapy alone is not curative, and that combined-modality approaches are needed to improve survival.
The main takeaway from our work is that
radiation therapy is a critical component of treatment for patients with unresectible stage IIIA and IIB NSCLC.

the use of high-dose radiation in combination with induction chemotherapy can result in improved local control rates and improved survival for patients with unresected stage III non-small cell lung carcinoma.

the use of high-dose, hypofractionated radiation therapy in combination with chemotherapy is an effective treatment for locally advanced non-small cell lung carcinoma, particularly when the patient's tumor is bulky.
